content:
While trying to update Carleson to latest Mathlib, I encountered some friction due to the (awesome!) fact that Set is now a one-field structure. I wanted to ask what are the best practices here. A basic example is that the lemma docs#MeasurableSet.biUnion (saying that MeasurableSet (⋃ b ∈ s, f b)) is applied to a union of the form ⋃ (i : ℕ) (hi : p i), s i. It used to work, now it doesn't, and that's perfectly expected.

Two questions: do we have/need a lemma rewriting ⋃ (i : ℕ) (hi : p i), s i to ⋃ i ∈ {i | p i}, s i? And should we change docs#MeasurableSet.biUnion (and many other lemmas) to not talk about ⋃ b ∈ s, f b but instead about ⋃ (i) (hi : p i), s i, which is now strictly more general?

While trying to update Carleson to latest Mathlib

Just checking to be sure: you're aware of Carleson#665, right? (Current plan is to merge Carleson#683 first, then update the PR accordingly, and merge that. Both are on my very-near-term TODO list.)
No, I wasn't aware, but I'm really happy about it!
If you want generality then p should return any Sort* and should be passed to f. I think this is then called iUnion₂ instead of biUnion, see docs#Set.mem_biUnion and docs#Set.mem_iUnion₂
out of curiosity, what is the benefit of making Set a one-field structure as opposed to just the function type into Prop as before?
It means that given (s : Set Nat) (n : Nat), it is a type error to write s n
ahhhh, fair point

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

do we have/need a lemma rewriting ⋃ (i : ℕ) (hi : p i), s i to ⋃ i ∈ {i | p i}, s i? And should we change docs#MeasurableSet.biUnion (and many other lemmas) to not talk about ⋃ b ∈ s, f b but instead about ⋃ (i) (hi : p i), s i, which is now strictly more general?

It seems a bit tedious to support both i ∈ {i | p i} and (i) (hi : p i), when the latter is already more readable/generic. Is it possible to have a simp lemma converting everything into ⋃ (i : ℕ) (hi : p i), s i as the normal form, and then write all of our theorems for this?
The former is already a particular case of the latter.
(with p := fun i => i ∈ {i | p i})

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

should we change docs#MeasurableSet.biUnion (and many other lemmas) to not talk about ⋃ b ∈ s, f b but instead about ⋃ (i) (hi : p i), s i, which is now strictly more general?

Indeed that is the correct fix. I did so already for the cases that appeared during the refactor, and it looks like no application of MeasurableSet.biUnion broke during the refactor.
Would you keep the name with biUnion and change the content, or add a new lemma mentioning iUnion₂?
I would keep biUnion because iUnion\_2 would instead be iUnion iterated twice (note how biUnion is not that due to differing countability assumptions!)

You could argue that

(hs : s.Countable) (h : ∀ b ∈ s, MeasurableSet (f b)) :
MeasurableSet (⋃ b ∈ s, f b)

should be written

(hs : {b | P b}.Countable) (h : ∀ b, P b -> MeasurableSet (f b)) :
MeasurableSet (⋃ b, ⋃ _ : P b, f b)

since the conclusion is syntactically more general
Yes, that's exactly what Sébastien and I are agreeing on above
Ah, so to to be clear: you're saying that my spelling should claim the name biUnion?

I thought biUnion specifically refers to using the fancy notation ⋃ x ∈ s, ...
Is the suggestion to unify biUnion and iUnion₂?

No, biUnion is the special case of iUnion\_2 where
the inner index is a Prop (and usually depends on the outer index)

Is the claim that we should always have biUnion for convenience (eg, to ensure rewrites only match prop binders without needing .{0}), or that we should only have it when additional assumptions are needed that only make sense for Prop?
Latter
#45097
This is really a big readability regression :sad:
Does "this" refer to #45097 or the full refactor?
Surely it's the PR, which replaces sets with maps to Prop and then has to build the sets anyway
The specific PR of course.
